question: How long is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
The waiting period for pre-existing diseases (PED) is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer [C140]. Important conditions and exceptions include:
- If the Sum Insured is enhanced, the exclusion applies afresh to the extent of the increase [C140].
- If you are continuously covered without a break based on IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by the prior coverage [C140].
- Coverage after 36 months is subject to the pre-existing disease being declared at application and accepted by the insurer [C140].

citations.label: Clause Excl01 - STANDARD EXCLUSIONS 1. Pre-Existing Diseases

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C72]. However, expenses related to the treatment of cataract are subject to a specified disease waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy, unless the claim arises due to an accident [C141]. Additionally, expenses incurred on the treatment of cataract are subject to specific limits per eye and per policy period depending on your Sum Insured [C72].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: Is there a limit on how much is paid for cataract treatment?
answer_en:
Yes, expenses incurred on the treatment of cataract are subject to specific limits based on your Sum Insured, per eye and per Policy Period [C72]. Furthermore, cataract treatment is subject to a 24-month waiting period of continuous coverage from the inception of the first policy, unless the claim arises due to an accident [C141].

Here are the limits per eye and per Policy Period according to the Sum Insured table [C72]:
- Sum Insured of Rs. 1,00,000/-: Up to 12,000/- per eye, per Policy Period [C72].
- Sum Insured of Rs. 3,00,000/-: Up to 25,000/- per eye, and up to 35,000/- per Policy Period [C72].
- Sum Insured of Rs. 4,00,000/-: Up to 30,000/- per eye, and up to 45,000/- per Policy Period [C72].
- Sum Insured of Rs. 5,00,000/-: Up to 40,000/- per eye, and up to 60,000/- per Policy Period [C72].
- Sum Insured of Rs. 10,00,000/-: Up to 50,000/- per eye, and up to 75,000/- per Policy Period [C72].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: Can I claim for an illness in the first month after buying the policy?
answer_en: No, expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date are excluded [C143]. However, claims arising due to an accident are covered, provided they are otherwise covered [C143]. This 30-day waiting period does not apply if you have continuous coverage for more than twelve months [C143].

question: For how many days before hospitalisation are medical expenses covered?
answer_en: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for a period not exceeding 60 days prior to the date of hospitalization, provided they are incurred for the disease/illness or injury sustained following an admissible claim for hospitalization under the policy [C76].

question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered?
answer_en: Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for a period of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C77]. These expenses must follow an admissible claim for hospitalization and be in respect of the same ailment for which the insured person was hospitalized [C77].

question: How much does the policy pay for a road ambulance?
answer_en: For a road ambulance, the policy pays up to Rs. 750/- per hospitalization and up to Rs. 1,500/- per Policy Period, subject to an admissible hospitalization claim [C78]. This applies to private ambulance service transportation to a hospital for medical reasons, from one hospital to another for better treatment, or from the hospital to the place of residence in the same city if certified by a medical practitioner [C78].

question: Are organ donor expenses covered, and is there a limit?
answer_en: Organ donor expenses for organ transplantation are covered when the Insured Person is the recipient, provided the claim for transplantation is payable and subject to the availability of the Sum Insured [C83]. However, donor screening expenses and post-donation complications of the donor are not payable [C83]. This cover is limited to 10% of the Sum Insured or Rupees One lakh, whichever is less [C83].

citations.label: Clause 11 - Organ Donor Expenses for organ

question: How soon must I inform the insurer after an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: For an emergency hospitalization (whether cashless or reimbursement), you must inform the insurer within 24 hours of the date and time of hospitalization [C179][C176].

citations.label: Clause B - Documents for Cashless Treatment

question: What is the deadline to file a reimbursement claim after discharge?
answer_en:
The deadlines to file a reimbursement claim after discharge are:
- For reimbursement of hospitalization, day care, and pre-hospitalization expenses: The claim must be filed within 15 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C178].
- For reimbursement of post-hospitalization expenses: The claim must be filed within 15 days after the completion of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C178].
Note that the company may examine and relax these time limits depending upon the merits of the case [C181].

question: Is cosmetic surgery covered?
answer_en: Cosmetic or plastic surgery and treatments to change appearance are generally not covered [C148]. However, they are covered if they are for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s), or Cancer, or as part of a medically necessary treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured [C148]. For it to be considered a medical necessity, it must be certified by the attending Medical Practitioner [C148].

citations.label: Clause Excl08 - Cosmetic or plastic Surgery

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The free look period is applicable on new individual health insurance policies with a term of one year or more, and does not apply to renewals or porting/migrating the policy [C197]. The Policyholder has a free look period of 30 days from the date of receipt of the policy document (electronically or otherwise) to review the terms and conditions [C197]. If the Policyholder is not satisfied and has not made any claim, they have the option to cancel the policy [C197]. Upon cancellation, they are entitled to a refund of the premium paid, subject to a deduction for a proportionate risk premium for the cover period, any expenses incurred by the insurer for a medical examination of the proposer, and stamp duty charges [C197].

question: How many times can the sum insured be restored in a policy year?
answer_en: The sum insured can be automatically restored 3 times at 100% each time during the Policy Period [C88]. This restoration happens immediately upon the exhaustion of the Limit of Coverage [C88]. It is available only for Sum Insured options of Rs. 3,00,000/- and above, and the restored amount can only be used for an illness or disease unrelated to previous claims [C88][C89].

citations.label: Clause 15 - Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured

question: Is knee replacement surgery covered from day one?
answer_en: No, knee replacement surgery (arthroplasty/joint replacement) is generally not covered from day one. Expenses related to treatments for bones and joint diseases, including arthroscopy and arthroplasty/joint replacement, are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception [C141]. However, this waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an accident [C141].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
The standard waiting period for pre-existing diseases (PED) is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer, unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule [C122]. Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease and its direct complications are excluded during this period [C122]. 

However, there are a few important conditions and modifications:
* **Optional Covers:** You can modify the PED waiting period to either 24 months (2 years) or 12 months (1 year) if you choose the optional PED waiting period modification cover at the time of policy inception [C114].
* **Sum Insured Enhancement:** If the Sum Insured is enhanced, the waiting period applies afresh to the extent of the increase in the Sum Insured [C122].
* **Portability:** If you are continuously covered without any break under portability norms, the waiting period will be reduced to the extent of your prior coverage [C122].
* **Declaration:** Coverage after 36 months is subject to the pre-existing disease being declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer [C122].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en:
Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C123]. However, it is subject to a specified disease/procedure waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy [C122][C123]. 

- The 24-month waiting period does not apply if the claim arises due to an accident [C122]. 
- There is also an initial 30-day waiting period for any illness from the first policy commencement date [C124], but the longer 24-month waiting period applies to specified conditions like cataract [C122][C123].

question: When will knee replacement surgery be covered?
answer_en: Joint replacement surgeries, which include knee replacement, are subject to a 24-month waiting period of continuous coverage after the first policy inception date [C124][C122]. Expenses related to this are excluded until this period expires, unless the claim arises due to an accident [C122]. If there is an enhancement of the Sum Insured, the waiting period applies afresh to the increased amount [C122]. Continuity benefits may reduce the waiting period if the insured person was previously covered without a break [C122].

question: Is there a room rent limit?
answer_en:
Yes, there is a room rent limit depending on your policy schedule and plan:

* **Default Limit:** Room rent is generally 'At Actuals' unless otherwise specified in your Policy Schedule [C80].
* **Proportionate Deduction:** If you are admitted in a room that exceeds the category or limit stipulated in your Policy Schedule, the reimbursement for room rent and associated medical expenses will be reduced proportionately based on the admissible rate versus the actual rate [C82].
* **Plan Modifications / Optional Covers:** Depending on your specific plan or optional covers chosen (such as Optima Lite, Optima Select, or the Modification of Room Rent option), room rent may be limited to up to 1% of the base sum insured per day, a Single Private room, or a Shared room [C115][C116][C184].

question: How soon must I notify the insurer of an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: For an emergency hospitalization, you must notify the insurer within 24 hours from the date of the emergency hospitalization or before the insured person's discharge from the hospital, whichever is earlier [C164]. Any delay in notification may be condoned on merits if the delay is proved to be for reasons beyond your control [C173].

question: How early should I inform the insurer before a planned hospitalisation?
answer_en: You should inform the insurer at least 48 hours prior to admission in the hospital in case of a planned hospitalization or a decision to avail treatment under Home Health Care [C164].

question: Within how many days must I submit documents for a reimbursement claim?
answer_en:
The time limit to submit documents for a reimbursement claim depends on the type of claim [C170]:
* **Hospitalization, Day Care Treatment, or Pre-Hospitalization Expenses:** Within 30 days of the date of discharge from the hospital [C170].
* **Post-Hospitalization Expenses:** Within 15 days from the completion of post-hospitalization treatment [C170].
* **Note:** Any delay in notification or submission may be condoned on merit if the delay is proven to be for reasons beyond the control of the insured person [C173].

question: How much cumulative bonus do I get on renewal?
answer_en: On renewal of your policy without a break, you receive a cumulative bonus (CB) provided as an increase in the Sum Insured without an associated increase in premium [C13][C89]. For 'Optima Suraksha' and 'Optima Lite' plans, the bonus is 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring policy per year, up to a maximum of 100% [C89][C182]. For the 'Optima Select' plan, it is 25% of the Base Sum Insured up to a maximum of 100% [C119][C182]. This is provided irrespective of any claims [C89][C182], but is subject to the policy being renewed or the premium being paid within the grace period [C90].

citations.label: Clause 1.8 - Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to ‘Optima Suraksha’, ‘Optima Lite’ and ‘Optima

question: Does the policy restore the sum insured after a claim?
answer_en:
Yes, the policy restores the sum insured through the Automatic Restore Benefit [C99].

* The company instantly adds 100% of the Base Sum Insured if an admissible claim partially or completely exhausts the sum insured during the Policy Year [C99].
* It is applied once during the Policy Year, unless 'Unlimited Times' is specified in the Policy Schedule [C100].
* The restored amount can only be used for subsequent claims during the remainder of that Policy Year and is restricted to Base Coverage and Protect Benefit claims [C100].
* Unutilized restored sum insured cannot be carried forward to subsequent years [C100].

citations.label: C100 - Specific Conditions applicable to Automatic Restore Benefit

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The free look period is thirty days from the date of receipt of the policy document [C138]. It applies only to new individual health insurance policies and not to renewals, porting, or migrating [C138]. During this time, the insured can review the terms and conditions and return the policy if it is not acceptable [C138]. If no claim has been made, the insured is entitled to a refund of the premium paid minus any medical examination expenses and stamp duty charges, a deduction for the proportionate risk premium if the risk has commenced, or a proportionate premium commensurate with the coverage if only part of the coverage has commenced [C138].

question: Are childbirth and maternity expenses covered in the base policy?
answer_en: This policy document does not cover childbirth and maternity expenses in the base policy. Maternity expenses and related treatments are listed separately under Parenthood as an optional plan chart cover [C192], which is not part of the base coverage clauses [C80].

question: Is plastic surgery to improve appearance covered?
answer_en: Plastic surgery to improve appearance is generally excluded under the policy [C126]. Expenses for cosmetic or plastic surgery or any treatment to change appearance are not covered, unless it is for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s), or Cancer, or as part of a Medically Necessary Treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured [C126]. For this medical necessity, it must be certified by the attending Medical Practitioner [C126]. Additionally, plastic surgery necessitated due to injury is covered up to the sum insured according to the plan chart and base coverage details [C81][C181].

citations.label: Clause Excl04 - Standard Exclusions a. Investigation & Evaluation (continued)

question: Is Ayurvedic treatment covered?
answer_en: Yes, Ayurvedic treatment is covered under the policy, but only for Inpatient Care and during each Policy Year up to the Sub-limit specified against this cover in the Policy Schedule, in any AYUSH Hospital [C85]. AYUSH Treatment refers to medical and/or hospitalisation treatments given under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy systems [C54].

question: How long do I wait before pre-existing diseases are covered?
answer_en:
Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications are excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer [C104]. 

Important conditions and exceptions apply:
- If you enhance the Sum Insured, the exclusion applies afresh to the extent of the increase [C104].
- If you are continuously covered without a break under portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by the prior coverage [C104].
- Coverage after 36 months is subject to the disease being declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer [C104].
- You can also choose to reduce or completely remove the Pre-Existing Disease waiting time by opting for the Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Time Modification benefit [C102].

citations.label: Clause Excl01 - Exclusions 5.1. Standard Exclusions 5.1.1. Pre-existing Diseases

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered [C105]. However, expenses related to its treatment are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C105]. This waiting period can be reduced if you have prior continuous coverage without a break under portability norms [C105]. If cataract falls under a pre-existing disease waiting period, the longer of the two waiting periods applies [C105].

question: When is knee replacement covered?
answer_en: Expenses related to joint replacement are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C105]. However, this waiting period applies afresh to the extent of any sum insured increase [C105], and if it falls under the waiting period for pre-existing diseases, the longer of the two waiting periods applies [C105]. If you are continuously covered without a break under IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by the prior coverage [C105].

question: Does the 24-month specific disease waiting period apply to cancer treatment?
answer_en: No, the 24-month specific disease waiting period does not apply to cancer treatment [C105]. Specifically, the policy states that the 24-month specified disease waiting period exclusion shall not be applicable for claims arising due to Cancer (covered after a 30-day waiting period) [C105].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease/procedure waiting period

question: How many days before and after hospitalisation are expenses covered?
answer_en: Expenses incurred on consultations, medicines, physiotherapy, and diagnostic tests are covered for 60 days before the date of admission and 180 days after the date of discharge, provided they are related to the condition for which the hospitalization claim is paid [C53].

citations.label: Clause 4.3 - Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)

question: Is there a restriction on the hospital room I can choose?
answer_en: There is no limit on your choice of room, and you can choose the room you like, but you should choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured [C49]. You can choose between a Single Private Room and a Sharing Room, and once chosen, this cannot be changed [C103]. However, if you opt for a hospital room higher than the eligible room category specified in your Policy Schedule, we will pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses based on the formula: (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses [C153].

citations.label: Clause 4.2.1 - We will pay the expenses incurred by you…

question: Is road ambulance covered, and up to how much?
answer_en:
Yes, road ambulance is covered. The policy will pay up to the Base Sum Insured [C46]. However, this is subject to the following conditions:
- The claim for hospitalization must be paid by the insurer [C48].
- You must always use a registered ambulance provider [C48].

question: What does ReAssure Forever do?
answer_en:
ReAssure “Forever” provides an unlimited Sum Insured under the policy [C62]. The feature is triggered by the first paid claim in the life of the policy and stays for life, as long as the policy is renewed without a break [C62]. 

Important conditions and limits apply:
* The maximum amount ReAssure “Forever” pays for any single claim is up to the Base Sum Insured [C63].
* A claim is considered when paid under expenses in reaching a hospital, hospitalization expenses, pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, home care / domiciliary treatment, or organ donor [C63][C64].
* Expenses in reaching a hospital and pre- and post-hospitalization expenses for the very first hospitalization are treated as the first claim itself [C64].

citations.label: C64 - and after hospitalization, Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment, Organ Donor.

question: What happens to the sum insured I don't use in a year?
answer_en: Under the Booster+ benefit, your unutilized Base Sum Insured carries forward [C72]. It can accumulate up to a maximum of 3, 5, or 10 times the Base Sum Insured, depending on the plan you have chosen [C72].

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The Free Look Period is applicable on new individual health insurance policies and is not applicable on renewals or when porting or migrating the policy [C128]. The insured person is allowed a free look period of 15 days (or 30 days for policies with a term of 3 years if sold through distance marketing) from the date of receipt of the policy document to review the terms and conditions and to return the policy if not acceptable [C128]. If no claim has been made during the Free Look Period, the insured is entitled to a refund of the premium paid, less any expenses incurred by the Company on the insured person's medical examination [C128].

question: Is LASIK surgery to remove my glasses covered?
answer_en: LASIK surgery to correct eyesight due to refractive errors is covered only if the refractive error is 7.5 dioptres or more [C116]. Expenses related to treatment for refractive errors less than 7.5 dioptres are excluded [C116].

question: Within how many days must I submit reimbursement claim documents?
answer_en: All claim documents must be submitted within 30 days from discharge [C153]. For any delay in submission, you must provide reasons in writing, and the company will condone such delay on merits for reasons beyond your control [C153].

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
The standard waiting period for pre-existing diseases (PED) is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer [C120]. 

Important conditions and exceptions apply:
- If you choose the Optional Benefit for PED Wait Period Modification, this waiting period can be modified to a specific time period mentioned in the Policy Schedule [C97].
- In case of an enhancement of the sum insured, the exclusion applies afresh to the extent of the sum insured increase [C120].
- If you are continuously covered without any break under portability norms, the waiting period is reduced to the extent of prior coverage [C120].
- Coverage after 36 months is subject to the pre-existing disease being declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer [C120].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C121]. However, it is subject to a named ailment waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy with the Company [C120]. If cataract is also considered a pre-existing disease and falls under the pre-existing disease waiting period, the longer of the two waiting periods shall apply [C120].

question: Is knee replacement covered and when?
answer_en: Yes, knee replacement (listed under joint replacement surgery) is covered under the policy [C121]. However, expenses related to it are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy with the Company, unless the claim arises due to an accident [C120][C121]. Furthermore, if you are continuously covered without a break under portability norms, the waiting period will be reduced to the extent of prior coverage [C121].

question: Is there any room rent limit?
answer_en:
Yes, under the base benefits for "Hospitalization Expenses", the eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the insured person is 'No limit', meaning there is no separate restriction on room charges incurred during hospitalization . Similarly, Intensive Care Unit (ICU) charges have 'No limit', with no separate restriction on ICU stay charges .

However, if the Optional Benefit "Room Rent Modification" is opted, the company agrees to modify the room rent or room category to a Single Private AC room or Twin sharing room as specified in the policy schedule [C95]. If you are admitted to a room with a higher rent or category than specified, you must bear a ratable proportion of the total associate medical expenses [C95]. Under this optional benefit, there is still no limit on ICU charges [C96].

question: For how many days before admission are medical expenses covered?
answer_en: Medical expenses are covered for a period of 60 days immediately prior to the insured person's date of admission to the hospital, provided they are medically necessary, incurred during the policy year, related to the same illness or injury for which the company accepted the hospitalization claim, and only through the reimbursement facility [C84].

question: How long after discharge are post-hospitalisation expenses covered?
answer_en:
Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for a period of 180 days immediately after the insured person's date of discharge from the hospital [C84].

Important conditions:
- The expenses must be medically necessary and incurred only through the reimbursement facility, up to the sum insured [C84].
- They must be related to the same illness or injury for which the company has accepted a claim under the 'Hospitalization Expenses' benefit [C84].
- Claim documents must be submitted within 30 days after the completion of 180 days from the date of discharge [C84].

question: How does the cumulative bonus work?
answer_en:
A Cumulative Bonus is an increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium [C10]. Here is how it works:

* **Accrual:** At the end of each Policy Year, the Company enhances the Sum Insured by 50% flat, on a cumulative basis, for each completed and continuous Policy Year [C88].
* **Cap:** The accrued Cumulative Bonus cannot exceed 100% of the Sum Insured available in the expiring Policy or renewed Policy, whichever is lower [C88].
* **Claims:** Filing a claim does not impact the accrual of the Cumulative Bonus [C88].
* **Forfeiture:** The entire Cumulative Bonus is forfeited if the Policy is not continued or renewed on or before the Policy Period End Date or the expiry of the Grace Period, whichever is later [C88].
* **Utilization:** Accrued Cumulative Bonus can be used for Base Benefits like 'Hospitalization Expenses' and 'Road Ambulance Cover' [C89].
* **Changes in Sum Insured:** If the Sum Insured is reduced at renewal, the Cumulative Bonus is reduced in proportion; if increased, it is calculated on the Sum Insured applicable on the last completed Policy Year [C89].

citations.label: Clause 2.1.8 - Cumulative Bonus mean any increase or

question: Is the sum insured recharged after it is used up?
answer_en:
Yes, the policy includes an "Unlimited Automatic Recharge" benefit. If a claim is payable, the company will automatically reinstate up to the base Sum Insured an unlimited number of times within that policy year, subject to the following conditions:
- The recharge can only be used after the base Sum Insured, applicable Cumulative Bonus, Cumulative Bonus Super (if applicable), and Plus Benefit (if applicable) are completely exhausted [C90].
- A claim is admissible under the recharge only if it is also admissible under "Hospitalization Expenses" [C90].
- The recharge amount can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses [C90].
- The recharged sum insured can only be used for "Hospitalization Expenses" and "Road Ambulance Cover" [C90].
- Any unutilized recharge cannot be carried forward to any subsequent policy year [C90].

question: How soon must I inform the insurer after an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: In case of an emergency hospitalization, you must notify the company either at their call center or in writing immediately, and in any event within 48 hours of the hospitalization commencing or before the insured person's discharge from the hospital [C179]. This notification is a condition precedent to the admission of liability under the policy [C179].

question: What is the deadline to file a claim after discharge?
answer_en: The claim must be filed within 30 days from the date of discharge from the hospital in case of hospitalization [C178]. Similarly, under the reimbursement facility, all information and documentation must be submitted within 30 days of the insured person's discharge from the hospital [C176].

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The Free Look Period applies to new individual health insurance policies and not to renewals, porting, or migrating [C158]. If you have not made any claim during this period, you are entitled to a refund of the premium paid less any medical examination expenses and stamp duty charges, a deduction for proportionate risk premium if the risk has commenced, or a proportionate premium corresponding to the coverage if only part of the coverage has commenced [C158].

question: Does this policy pay for childbirth expenses?
answer_en: This policy defines maternity expenses to include medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth (including complicated deliveries and caesarean sections incurred during hospitalization) and expenses towards lawful medical termination of pregnancy during the policy period [C26]. However, under the standard exclusions, maternity expenses—including medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth and caesarean sections, except for ectopic pregnancy—are generally excluded from coverage [C138]. Miscarriage expenses are also excluded unless due to an accident [C138].

question: ముందుగా ఉన్న వ్యాధులకు వేచి ఉండే కాలం ఎంత?
answer_en: The waiting period for Pre-Existing Diseases (PED) is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer, unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule [C122]. This may be reduced based on prior continuous coverage or portability norms [C122].
answer: ముందుగా ఉన్న వ్యాధులకు (Pre-Existing Diseases - PED) వేచి ఉండే కాలం మొదటి విధానం అమలోకి వచ్చిన తేదీ నుండి నిరంతర కవరేజీతో 36 నెలలు [C122]. విధాన షెడ్యూల్‌లో ప్రత్యేకంగా పేర్కొనకపోతే, ఈ కాలం వర్తిస్తుంది [C122]. నిరంతర కవరేజీని బట్టి లేదా పోర్టబిలిటీ నిబంధనల ప్రకారం ఇది మారవచ్చు [C122].

question: क्या इस पॉलिसी में कमरे के किराए की कोई सीमा है?
answer_en: Under this policy, there is no separate restriction on room charges incurred towards stay during hospitalization, as the eligible room rent or room category applicable for the insured person is 'No limit' [C86]. Additionally, there is no limit on ICU charges under the policy [C86]. However, if the optional benefit 'Room Rent Modification' is opted, the room category/rent is limited to a Single Private AC room or Twin sharing room as specified in the Policy Schedule [C95], and if a higher room category is chosen, a proportional deduction of associate medical expenses will apply [C95][C182].
answer: इस पॉलिसी के तहत कमरे के किराए पर कोई अलग से प्रतिबंध नहीं है, क्योंकि पॉलिसी के तहत लागू कमरे का किराया या कमरा श्रेणी 'कोई सीमा नहीं' (No limit) है [C86]। इसके अलावा, इस पॉलिसी के तहत आईसीयू (ICU) शुल्क पर भी कोई सीमा नहीं है [C86]। हालांकि, यदि वैकल्पिक लाभ (Optional Benefit) के रूप में 'रूम रेंट मॉडिफिकेशन' चुना जाता है, तो कमरे का किराया या कमरा श्रेणी पॉलिसी शेड्यूल में निर्दिष्ट के अनुसार सिंगल प्राइवेट एसी रूम या ट्विन शेयरिंग रूम तक सीमित हो सकती है [C95], और यदि इससे उच्च श्रेणी का कमरा लिया जाता है, तो आनुपातिक कटौती लागू होगी [C95][C182]।

question: రోడ్ అంబులెన్స్ ఖర్చులు ఎంత వరకు చెల్లిస్తారు?
answer_en: Road ambulance expenses are payable up to Rs.750/- per hospitalization and up to Rs.1,500/- per Policy Period, subject to an admissible hospitalization claim [C78]. This applies to transportation by private ambulance service to a hospital for medical reasons, from one hospital to another for better treatment, or from the hospital to the residence (if in the same city) with a medical practitioner's certification [C78].
answer: రోడ్ అంబులెన్స్ ఖర్చులు ఆమోదించదగిన ఆసుపత్రిలో చేరే క్లెయిమ్‌కు లోబడి, ప్రతి ఆసుపత్రిలో చేరడానికి రూ.750/- వరకు మరియు పాలసీ కాలవ్యవధికి రూ.1,500/- వరకు చెల్లించబడతాయి [C78]. ఇది ప్రైవేట్ అంబులెన్స్ సేవ ద్వారా వైద్య కారణాల వల్ల ఆసుపత్రికి వెళ్లడానికి, ఒక ఆసుపత్రి నుండి మెరుమైన వైద్యం కోసం మరొక ఆసుపత్రికి వెళ్లడానికి, లేదా వైద్యుని ధృవీకరణతో ఆసుపత్రి నుండి నివాసానికి (అదే నగరంలో ఉంటే) రవాణా చేయడానికి వర్తిస్తుంది [C78].

question: Is knee replacement covered and after how long?
answer_en: Knee replacement (joint replacement) is covered under the policy [C105]. Expenses related to its treatment are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C105].
answer: घुटने का प्रतिस्थापन (joint replacement) इस पॉलिसी के तहत कवर किया जाता है [C105]। इसके इलाज से संबंधित खर्चों पर पहली पॉलिसी शुरू होने की तारीख से 24 महीने की निरंतर कवरेज पूरी होने तक रोक रहती है [C105]।
